questions.prediction: The parent is expected to send 206 with bcd. The landing should return 200, abcdef and no Content-Range on each route.
questions.basis: The client's validator is stale. RFC 9110 requires ignoring the range so the client can replace its old representation.
questions.refutation: Any landed route emits a slice, a partial status or a Content-Range.

questions.history: Use the same Range with no If-Range, then with the matching strong "v2".
questions.prediction: Both revisions should return 206, Content-Range bytes 1-3/6 and the exact bytes bcd.
questions.basis: An inclusive range from offsets 1 through 3 selects three known bytes. Both requests authorize serving that range.
questions.refutation: Status or endpoints are wrong, or the body cannot be spliced back at offset 1.

questions.history: Keep the stale validator and replace the requested range with bytes=broken. Also try a syntactically valid range with W/"v2".
questions.prediction: At the landing both should return the entire abcdef and 200. In the first call ignoring the range also suppresses any range-parse failure.
questions.basis: The validator is evaluated before Range. Weak tags cannot authorize combining portions of representations.
questions.refutation: The malformed value yields 416 or the weak tag yields a partial body.

questions.history: Use a resource known to change at most once per second and an emitted Last-Modified value. Send that exact HTTP-date, then the valid date one second later, with bytes=1-3.
questions.prediction: The landing should return 206/bcd for the exact strong date and 200/abcdef for the later date. Before, expect 206/bcd for both.
questions.basis: If-Range date comparison is exact. A later date does not identify the representation used for a previous download.
questions.refutation: The exact date loses the range, or the later date is treated as fresh enough.
